pr_body: Do not ellipsize output when `-l` or `--full` is handed to `networkctl lldp`. Fixes #22806.

issue_context.title: systemd-networkd doesn't show full lldp information with networkctl lldp
issue_context.body:
I can reproduce the issue on the current debian stable and arch linux.

**systemd version the issue has been seen with**
```
$ systemd --version
systemd 247 (247.3-6)
+PAM +AUDIT +SELINUX +IMA +APPARMOR +SMACK +SYSVINIT +UTMP +LIBCRYPTSETUP +GCRYPT +GNUTLS +ACL +XZ +LZ4 +ZSTD +SECCOMP +BLKID +ELFUTILS +KMOD +IDN2 -IDN +PCRE2 default-hierarchy=unified
```
```
$ systemctl --version                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
systemd 250 (250.4-2-arch)
+PAM +AUDIT -SELINUX -APPARMOR -IMA +SMACK +SECCOMP +GCRYPT +GNUTLS +OPENSSL +ACL +BLKID +CURL +ELFUTILS +FIDO2 +IDN2 -IDN +IPTC +KMOD +LIBCRYPTSETUP +LIBFDISK +PCRE2 -PWQUALITY +P11KIT -QRENCODE +BZIP2 +LZ4 +XZ +ZLIB +ZSTD -BPF_FRAMEWORK +XKBCOMMON +UTMP -SYSVINIT default-hierarchy=unified
```

**Used distribution**
```
$ cat /etc/os-release
PRETTY_NAME="Debian GNU/Linux 11 (bullseye)"
NAME="Debian GNU/Linux"
VERSION_ID="11"
VERSION="11 (bullseye)"
VERSION_CODENAME=bullseye
ID=debian
HOME_URL="https://www.debian.org/"
SUPPORT_URL="https://www.debian.org/support"
BUG_REPORT_URL="https://bugs.debian.org/"
```
```
$ cat /etc/os-release
NAME="Arch Linux"
PRETTY_NAME="Arch Linux"
ID=arch
BUILD_ID=rolling
ANSI_COLOR="38;2;23;147;209"
HOME_URL="https://archlinux.org/"
DOCUMENTATION_URL="https://wiki.archlinux.org/"
SUPPORT_URL="https://bbs.archlinux.org/"
BUG_REPORT_URL="https://bugs.archlinux.org/"
LOGO=archlinux-logo
```

**Linux kernel version used** (`uname -a`)
```
$ uname -a
Linux tonno 5.10.0-7-amd64 #1 SMP Debian 5.10.40-1 (2021-05-28) x86_64 GNU/Linux
```
```
$ uname -a
Linux nyu 5.16.11-arch1-1 #1 SMP PREEMPT Thu, 24 Feb 2022 02:18:20 +0000 x86_64 GNU/Linux
```

**CPU architecture issue was seen on**
```
$ lscpu | head -1
Architecture:                    x86_64
```

**Expected behaviour you didn't see**
I would expect a full output of the lldp info like `GigabitEthernet1/0/10`.

**Unexpected behaviour you saw**
A shortened version of the info that always cuts off after a fixed number of chars e.g. `GigabitEthernet1...`.

Example output:

```
$ networkctl lldp
LINK             CHASSIS ID        SYSTEM NAME      CAPS        PORT ID           PORT DESCRIPTION
eno3             ff:00:00:bb:aa:aa core.home.netwk  ..b.r...... GigabitEthernet1… GigabitEthernet…
eno4             ff:00:00:bb:aa:aa core.home.netwk  ..b.r...... GigabitEthernet2… GigabitEthernet…

Capability Flags:
b - Bridge; r - Router

2 neighbors listed.
```

**Steps to reproduce the problem**
Connect device A via ethernet to device B (other pc, switch, router, etc) that supports LLDP and set lldp information on device B that exceed 16 characters for port id and/or description. Then issue `networkctl lldp` command on device A to see shortened output.

**Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue**

<!-- Please paste relevant program terminal or journal output here, ideally
     when generated in debug mode (try setting the SYSTEMD_LOG_LEVEL=debug
     environment variable). For very long copy/pasted data consider using a
     service like https://gist.github.com/. Where copy/paste is not possible
     (for example early boot or late shutdown), a photo of the screen might do
     too, but text is always much preferred. -->
```
$ env SYSTEMD_LOG_LEVEL=debug networkctl lldp
Successfully forked off '(pager)' as PID 1506181.
Skipping PR_SET_MM, as we don't have privileges.
Found cgroup2 on /sys/fs/cgroup/, full unified hierarchy
Pager executable is "pager", options "FRSXMK", quit_on_interrupt: yes
LINK             CHASSIS ID        SYSTEM NAME      CAPS        PORT ID           PORT DESCRIPTION
eno3             ff:00:00:bb:aa:aa core.home.netwk  ..b.r...... GigabitEthernet1… GigabitEthernet…
eno4             ff:00:00:bb:aa:aa core.home.netwk  ..b.r...... GigabitEthernet2… GigabitEthernet…

Capability Flags:
b - Bridge; r - Router

2 neighbors listed.
```

review_comments:
In the above, we have
```
        if (arg_full)
                table_set_width(table, 0);
```
and table_add_many() ellipsizes strings gracefully.

Hence, please unconditionally put the given strings, e.g. chassis_id, to the table.

Oh, so you mean all this ellipsizing code from line 2555 to 2578 is superfluous since `table_add_many()` ellipsizes strings anyway? I just tried it by commenting those lines out but nothing is ellipsized in my table.

See,
https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/c87c30780624df257ed96909a2286b2b933f8c44/src/shared/format-table.c#L136-L137
And, by default, the width is SIZE_MAX. Hence, each strings are truncated if you run the command on a terminal with short width.

Ok, but as I said: Nothing is truncated on my shell when I set it to 60 characters and remove those calls to `ellipsize()`, i.e., `ellipsize(chassis_id, 17, 100)` and so on. So either your claim is wrong or something else is going on.
Please provide the diff you tested.
Maybe, `table_set_minimum_width()` in the above is too large for your terminal width?

Even with a width of `145` the table overflows as no string in any column is truncated. I have one very long name in the column `SYSTEM NAME`. Please try it out yourself, the column formatting definitely works not as expected.
